title: Gaussia luciferase blood level as an index of cell growth and proliferation
protocol: Subclone the Gluc cDNA into a viral vector using standard cloning protocols.
Transduce cells with lentivirus vectors under conditions that ensure high efficiency.
Clone the Gaussia luciferase cDNA and a fluorescent protein such as GFP, separated by an IRES element, into a lentivirus vector.
Place these elements under the control of the strong constitutive CMV promoter to produce LV-Gluc-GFP.
Plate one million cells in a 2 cm² well.
Add lentivirus vector to achieve an MOI of 10 - 50 in the presence of 8 μg/ml polybrene after 24 hours.
Wash the cells with PBS after 5 hours.
Add fresh culture medium and incubate the cells for 48 hours.
Alternatively, transfect the cells using plasmid expressing Gluc with lipofectamine.
Determine transduction/transfection efficiency by analyzing CFP expression using fluorescence microscopy.
Harvest 5 - 20 μl aliquots of conditioned medium into a clean white or black 96-well plate.
Measure Gluc activity using a plate luminometer set to inject 50 μl of 20 μM coelenterazine in DMEM and acquire photon counts for 10 seconds.
Grow and freeze the cells if lentivirus vector was used for stable expression.
Aliquot 10 μl of conditioned medium into a black or white plate.
Measure Gluc activity after injecting 50 μl of 20 μM coelenterazine.
Acquire signal for 10 sec using a luminometer.
Plate one to five thousand cells in a well of 96-well plate in triplicate.
Start taking 10 μl aliquots at different time points the next day.
Measure Gluc activity as above.
Dilute coelenterazine in DMEM and store at room temperature in the dark for 30 min before use.
Anesthetize mice by i.p. injection of ketamine (100 mg/kg) and xylazine (5 mg/kg).
Inject Gluc-expressing cells or Gluc-expression vectors at the location of interest or systemically (i.v.).
Withdraw blood samples from mice either through a tail incision or retro-orbitally.
Mix 2 μl EDTA with each 5 μl blood sample immediately after withdrawal and store at 4°C until all samples are collected.
Measure Gluc activity using a plate luminometer that injects 100 μl of stabilized coelenterazine (incubated for 30 min at room temperature in DMEM) into the blood samples.
Acquire photon counts for 10 sec from each sample to measure Gluc activity.
Dissolve coelenterazine in acidified methanol by adding a drop of concentrated HCl to 10 ml of methanol.
Prepare a solution of coelenterazine at a concentration of 4 mg/ml.
Anesthetize the mice as previously described.
Inject each anesthetized mouse intravenously with 150 μl of coelenterazine solution (4 mg/kg body weight).
Acquire photon counts over 1-5 minutes using a cooled CCD camera without illumination.
Take a light image of the animal in the chamber using dim polychromatic illumination.
Define regions of interest using an automatic intensity contour procedure to identify bioluminescence signals with intensities significantly greater than background.
Calculate the mean, standard deviation, and sum of photon counts in the defined regions as measurements of Gluc activity.
Fuse bioluminescence images with corresponding white light surface images for visualization.
Mix 20 μl of coelenterazine with 130 μl PBS immediately before injection.
Inject the mixed solution intravenously immediately after mixing.
If a small precipitate or cloudy solution forms during injection, continue with imaging as normal.
Do not incubate coelenterazine in PBS at room temperature to avoid larger precipitate formation.
Consider performing retro-ocular injections if tail vein injection is difficult.
Observe for any photons around the eye area post-injection and consider this normal due to injection method.
